eligibility_note: Own panel estimation (TWFE, C&D DiD, 2SLS) of mobile 2G/3G/4G coverage; 106-120 countries (>=10) with explicit developing vs developed income-group comparison. Outcome is district nightlight growth, which the paper uses as a proxy for local economic activity (Henderson et al. 2011, 2012). Reading it as a family-1 output proxy is acceptable: nightlights are a standard, validated proxy for subnational activity, and the paper itself says it measures activity, not GDP. Two caveats: lights can also capture electrification or lighting rather than value added, and the GDP elasticity of 0.018-0.023 is an external back-of-envelope conversion (0.3 from Henderson et al.), not an estimate. Eligibility holds; the nightlight outcome should be flagged as a proxy.

income_group_note: Developed (HIC+UMIC) 0.0510*** (col 2), 2G ns, 3G/4G 0.0868*** match Table 5. Developing 'about 0.09' is the sum 0.0510+0.0395; the paper reports only the '0.9 pp' in text and no SE for the sum, so the developing-group 2G and 3G/4G effects are derived and their significance is not reported. No separate LIC, LMIC or UMIC estimates, as the record states.

risk_of_bias.confounding_reverse_causation: agree (moderate): the author concedes TWFE/C&D are not causal (significant pre-trends, endogenous rollout) and uses a lagged regional leave-one-out IV with regional GDP/trade controls, but the exclusion restriction is contestable and IV estimates (0.0777) are about 6x TWFE (0.0136).
risk_of_bias.exposure_measurement: agree (moderate): operator-submitted coverage maps combined with population grids measure population covered, not adoption or use; 2005 and 2010 are interpolated.
risk_of_bias.selection_of_countries_years: agree (low): near-global district panel with leave-one-country-out check; sample shrinks from 120 to 106 (86 for 3G/4G) with controls but this is disclosed.
risk_of_bias.outcome_measurement: too_harsh (record says serious; moderate fits): district nightlight growth is a standard, validated proxy for local activity and the paper claims only that; the weakness is the electrification confound and the external 0.3 elasticity used for the GDP translation, which is flagged as derived.
risk_of_bias.specification: agree (moderate): several instruments, controls and technology splits with a stated preferred specification; estimates vary widely (A4 3G/4G about 0.29 vs 0.07 in Table 3).
risk_of_bias.selective_reporting: agree (low): null and pre-trend placebo failures are reported openly, though table labelling and notes are sloppy.
risk_of_bias.why: Credible-ish IV design with openly reported weaknesses and standard but not strongly exogenous identification; exogeneity not established, so moderate is right. Only the outcome domain is rated too harshly.

problems: Estimate field of result 1 is garbled but numbers are right. Result 2 is a derived conversion, not an estimate. Result 6 'positive' overlooks the null 3G/4G TWFE in col 5. Paper has typos (Table 1 panel labels, Table 5 note copied from Table 6, 'DIDpl,2' printed twice, DIDpl,2 3G/4G shows 0.0525*** and -0.0536*** in cols 5-6, as printed). Nothing invented or mixed with another paper. Venue is a World Bank working paper (PRWP 10526, July 2023). No instruction-like text in the paper.
